title: cross-functional-incident-ownership-and-hotseat-sop-2026
author: Nora Chen
body:
Overview

This page documents the cross-functional incident ownership model and the Hotseat Standard Operating Procedure (Hotseat SOP). The Hotseat is a temporary, time-boxed role that centralizes decision authority during multi-team incidents and noisy degradations. This SOP covers when to activate Hotseat, responsibilities, handoff steps, customer communication templates, and game-day exercises to validate the flow.

Goals and scope

- Reduce cognitive churn during cross-team incidents by naming a single Hotseat operator.
- Ensure predictable, auditable ownership transfers for incidents affecting: api-gateway, inference-runtime, cache-kv-service, and ingest-queue.
- Standardize customer-facing communications and quiet-window decisions.
- Excludes routine single-service alerts where a single service owner can resolve within 30 minutes.

When to activate Hotseat (decision ladder)

1) PagerDuty alert (P0 or sustained P1 > 20 min) impacting >10% of customer traffic OR causing sustained SLO deviation.
2) Multiple dependent services are affected (evidence from traces or topology).
3) Active cross-team coordination required (two or more engineering teams plus SRE/product).

Roles and responsibilities

- Hotseat Operator (hotseat): Named single point of decision-making for the incident window. Coordinates status cadence, approves customer comms, and drives mitigation decisions.
- Incident Lead (service-owner): Owns technical remediation and runbook steps for a specific service. Reports status to Hotseat every 10 minutes.
- Bridge Facilitator (ops): Operates the bridge (Zoom/Bridge) and ensures documentation of commands and timeline.
- Customer Liaison (cs): Crafts customer messaging with Hotseat approval and owns external stakeholder notifications.
- Escalation Support (eng-sre): Availability for extra capacity actions (global routing, infra resizes, emergency failover).

Ownership matrix (quick table)

Service | Primary owner | Secondary contact | Typical runbook
------- | ------------- | ----------------- | -----------------
api-gateway | Erica Park | Jonah Meyer | api-gateway/runbook-v3
inference-runtime | Rafael Ortiz | Mei Lin | runtime/latency-triage
cache-kv-service | Priya Desai | Kofi Mensah | storage/cache-kv-deg
ingest-queue | Omar Malik | Talia Rivera | ingest/queue-backpressure

Hotseat activation procedure (10-step checklist)

1. PagerDuty acknowledged by on-call; initial triage completed (impact, blast radius, tentative severity).
2. If triggers met, on-call posts to #ops-bridge: "Hotseat requested" and page Hotseat rotation.
3. Hotseat accepts within 5 minutes and creates incident thread in ticketing tool (INC-YYYYMMDD-###).
4. Bridge facilitator opens bridge and pins incident ticket.
5. Hotseat assigns Incident Lead(s) and confirms secondary contacts.
6. Establish 10-minute cadence updates and document next action every cadence.
7. If customer-impacting, Customer Liaison prepares first external note draft within 15 minutes.
8. Hotseat reviews and approves any mitigation that changes customer-visible behavior (rollbacks, rate limits).
9. When steady-state returns or failover completes, Hotseat transitions to Recovery mode and orders evidence collection.
10. Hotseat enters a formal handoff (see transfer checklist) before relinquishing role.

Hotseat transfer checklist (must be completed for every handoff)

- Time of handoff (UTC)
- Current severity and SLO deviation metrics (percent of impacted traffic)
- Active mitigations and who controls them (IP addresses, topology changes, flags)
- Known root causes or hypotheses and required actions
- Outstanding blockers and last attempted remediation command(s)
- Next check-in time and expected duration of new owner
- Incident ticket link and artifacts location (logs, traces, dashboards)

Example handoff note (paste to incident ticket)

Handoff from Hotseat Nora Chen -> Hotseat Liam O'Neill at 2026-02-18T16:30Z
- Severity: P1 (20% API error increase, 12% customer impact)
- Active mitigation: global rate-limit applied at edge (rule id: rl-8321)
- Next action: expand autoscaler pool + restart api-gateway pods in eu-west-1 (Jonah assigned)
- Evidence: link to trace span collection: https://dash/internal/trace/INC-12345

On-call rotation: Hotseat rotation pattern

- Hotseat is a 4-hour rotation sampled from SRE and Platform teams during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT). Outside business hours, the primary on-call acts as Hotseat unless escalated.
- Shift example: 08:00-12:00, 12:00-16:00, 16:00-20:00. Each team provides a nominated backup.
- Hotseat handover must complete with the checklist above; if incomplete, the outgoing Hotseat remains accountable until the transfer is complete.

Tactical shortcuts and guardrails

- Short-circuit: If a single service owner can remediate within 15 minutes with low risk, Hotseat deactivation is allowed. Document decision.
- Emergency rollback: Hotseat may authorize an emergency rollback to the last verified tag. Authorization must be recorded in the ticket.
- No unilateral customer data exports or escalations to sales without Customer Liaison consent.

Customer communication templates (concise, editable)

Template 1 - Initial acknowledgement (use within 30 minutes):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident affecting API latency — initial update
Body:
Hi {CustomerName},
We are investigating increased API latency affecting a subset of requests. Our team has identified an active incident and we will provide an update within 30 minutes. Impact: {approx_percent}% of requests.
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-12345
Regards,
Redwood Support Team

Template 2 - Actionable update (after mitigation):
Subject: [Redwood] Update: mitigation in progress for API latency
Body:
Hi {CustomerName},
We have applied a temporary rate-limit and resumed requests for most customers. You may see intermittent errors while we validate recovery. Next update in 20 minutes or sooner for major changes.
- Mitigation: rate-limit rl-8321 applied
- Expected next steps: expand pool; full rollback if instability persists
Regards,
{Customer Liaison}

Template 3 - Post-incident customer summary (sent after postmortem):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident summary and mitigation details — {date}
Body:
Hi {CustomerName},
Thank you for your patience. We experienced increased errors caused by {short root cause}. We have completed remediation and implemented these mitigations: 1) {fix1}, 2) {fix2}. We are sharing a full postmortem here: https://confluence/redwood/incidents/INC-12345
If you have any follow-ups, reply to this message and your Customer Liaison will assist.

Runbook template (to be copied into per-service runbooks)

Title: <service>-incident-triage
Preconditions: SLOs impacted > 5% or latency > 500ms 95th
Detection: Alerts from prom-alerts (alert id: prom/ticket) and error-rate > threshold
Initial steps:
1) Confirm alert and scope (use logs: kubectl logs -l app=<service> --since=15m)
2) Check dashboards: link to <service> 95th/99th latency and error-rate
3) Identify recent deploys: git rev-parse --short HEAD; kubectl rollout status
4) Apply canary rollback if deploy is suspected: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> --to-revision=<rev>
Mitigations:
- Scale pool: aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name <asg> --desired-capacity <n>
- Edge rate-limiting: curl -X POST https://edge-api/rules -d '{"rule":"<spec>"}'
Escalation: If unable to restore in 30 minutes, notify Hotseat and escalate to Eng SRE.

Game day exercises (quarterly)

Purpose: Validate Hotseat flows and transfer checklist under time pressure, specifically multi-service incidents that require cross-team coordination.
Frequency: Quarterly for SRE + Eng Platform + Product.
Example scenario: KV cache corruption in eu-west-1 causes inference-runtime timeouts and increased backpressure on ingest-queue.
Success criteria:
- Hotseat accepted within 5 minutes
- First external note drafted within 15 minutes
- Recovery to baseline latency within 60 minutes for primary traffic zone
- Complete postmortem draft within 72 hours

Postmortem and evidence requirements

- Initial incident summary posted within 24 hours.
- Full postmortem draft within 72 hours with: timeline, impact, root cause hypotheses, evidence (logs, traces, configs), remediation plan, owners, and action items with due dates.
- Severity change to P0 requires a compliance evidence package for legal and enterprise accounts: list of impacted customers, timelines, and retention of raw logs for 90 days.

KPIs & SLO thresholds referenced by Hotseat

- API success rate SLO: 99.90% (rolling 7d)
- Inference tail latency (95th): < 200ms for small payloads, < 700ms for long-run payloads
- KV cache availability SLO: 99.95%
- Hotseat acknowledgement SLA: 5 minutes during business hours

Evidence capture: commands & storage locations

- Always paste key commands in the incident ticket and mark them as code. Example: kubectl -n prod logs deploy/api-gateway --since=10m | grep ERROR
- Save trace snapshots to: https://traces.redwood.internal/snapshots/INC-12345
- Archive critical logs to s3://redwood-incident-archive/INC-12345/logs/ with encryption (KMS: rwd-incident-key).

Runbook retirement and maintenance

- Owners must review runbooks after any hotseat activation that used them (within 7 days).
- Annual cleanup: each runbook has a review_date metadata field and must be confirmed or retired at least once a year.

Appendix: Quick decision ladder (one-line commands)

- Add capacity: aws ec2 run-instances --count 6 --launch-template lt-abc123 (ops only)
- Revert deploy: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc>
- Apply temporary rate-limit: curl -X POST https://edge-api/rules -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_TOKEN' -d '{"rule":"deny-high-error"}'

Contacts and escalation roster

- Hotseat rotation lead (primary): eng-sre oncall schedule (see roster)
- PagerDuty escalation policy: Redwood-P0-Global
- Support: support@redwood.ai, Customer Liaison: cs-liaisons@redwood.ai
